messages:
olivia: Quick summary from the hetero-int8 vs nf4-v3 bring-up on rwdv7 chat. Main points:
- throughput ~1.8x on typical gen workloads
- delta MRR: -0.6% overall, but -1.4% on long-doc slice
- hallucination rate +0.3 percentage points on long-doc slice only
- median latency down ~15ms, p95 down ~120ms for hot paths
Thinking phased rollout: 5% canary -> 20% -> 100%, with a soft hold if hallucination delta > 0.5pp for 30m and auto-fallback to nf4 if sustained. Ping if you want raw CSVs. :eyes:

sam: Can you paste the per-slice numbers and the eval set names? also curious about kv-warmup mismatch (did you coldstart from empty cache?)

olivia: Pasted slices and small table below. We ran with cold KV for the long-doc slice to stress warmup. Short summary table:

```
slice            | MRR_base | MRR_het8 | delta_pp | halluc_base | halluc_het8 | p95_base | p95_het8
long-doc         | 0.743    | 0.729    | -1.4     | 0.9         | 1.2         | 420ms    | 300ms
shortchat        | 0.812    | 0.807    | -0.5     | 0.4         | 0.4         | 85ms     | 60ms
code-assist      | 0.676    | 0.672    | -0.4     | 0.2         | 0.3         | 110ms    | 70ms
```

Notes: we saw the long-doc regression concentrated on very long generation tails (>2048 tokens) and cold-KV scenarios.

anya: Thanks. Two asks: (1) add focused coverage on math/QA slices (they spike hallucinations differently), (2) add a fidelity probe that runs a deterministic set of prompts every 5m and fails the canary if exact-match on structured outputs drops.

mike: Memory/oom looks fine on our machines but token-per-second throughput dropped 10% on extreme-context cases (due to additional dequant step). Do we have quantized kernel fallback for those long contexts, or will we route to nf4?

olivia: For extreme contexts we saw an extra dequant/reshape cost. Plan is to route >4096 token sessions to nf4 variant automatically (policy-level). Shorter sessions stay on hetero-int8.

zoe: +1 to Anya. For user-facing search product we should tighten the soft hold: set hallucation delta threshold to 0.25pp (0.0025) and require 15m sustained window. Non-critical internal flows can be 0.5pp.

sam: Also recommend we add a shadow-run of nf4 on 10% of hetero-int8 traffic to keep a rolling comparison and detect drift fast.

olivia: Agreed. I'll create a rollout config and smoke eval. Draft canary config snippet below — will wire into Console & create a rollout job.

```json
{
  "canary_pct": 5,
  "staged_steps": [5, 20, 100],
  "fidelity_probe": {
    "promptset": "rwd_fidelity_v2",
    "interval_mins": 5,
    "exact_match_threshold": 0.99
  },
  "signals": [
    {"name": "halluc_rate","delta_threshold": 0.0025,"window_mins": 15,"action":"hold"},
    {"name": "mrr","delta_threshold": -0.005,"window_mins": 30,"action":"hold"}
  ],
  "auto_fallback": {"on_sustained_violation_mins": 30, "route_to": "nf4-v3"},
  "shadow_compare": {"pct": 10, "route_shadow_to": "nf4-v3"}
}
```

deploy-bot: Canary config saved and scheduled. Will start canary when rollout job is approved. :white_check_mark:

zoe: Please also add an alert to paging if hallucation delta > 1.0pp on primary product for 10m. Non-paging alerts OK for internal slices.

olivia: Will do. Tagging @eng-sre to validate alert thresholds and paging policy. I'll attach raw CSVs and the test harness next. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
